script: Good morning, it's Thursday 24 September. Here's your pre-open briefing. Wall Street had a softer session. The S&P 500 fell about seven tenths of a percent and the Nasdaq Composite about one point one percent. The biggest mover on our watchlist was Alphabet, down three point eight percent. There was no clear news behind that move, though one report noted the company's DeepMind chief said Gemini four is coming much earlier. Amazon was next, down two point two percent, and again there was nothing in the headlines that clearly explains the fall. Elsewhere the tone was mixed rather than uniformly weak. The big chipmakers drifted lower, the largest bank on the list eased, and the oil major and one social media name finished higher. Trading volumes were broadly ordinary, with a little more activity than usual in a couple of the megacap technology names. In London, the market was close to flat. The FTSE 100 slipped about one tenth of a percent, so the weakness seen in New York did not really carry through. The standout was BP, up two point nine percent. There was no clear news behind that move. Shell followed, up one point nine percent, after completing an eight hundred and forty million dollar sale of Gulf oil assets. Away from energy the mood was mildly negative. AstraZeneca gave back some ground, the big banks drifted lower, and the telecoms and consumer names were a touch weaker. There was no volume data available for the London names, so it is hard to say how much conviction sat behind any of these moves. Looking at Oceania today. The ASX two hundred opens at ten, with local futures pointing to a flat to slightly positive start. Australian job vacancies data lands at half past eleven, the quarterly release from the Bureau of Statistics, watched for signs of a cooling labour market. Miners are in focus all day, with overnight iron ore and copper moves setting the tone for BHP, Rio Tinto and Fortescue. In New Zealand, the monthly trade balance is due at a quarter to nine, before the NZX opens. This briefing is AI-generated general information only. It is not financial advice.
